decisive_items: Post-procedure peritonitis is supported by the temporal relationship to the procedure, fever, abdominal pain, CT findings of bowel wall edema and ascites, positive E. coli culture, and histology showing neutrophilic infiltration and abscesses. The absence of overt perforation on imaging does not exclude microperforation or contamination during ESD. Perforated appendicitis is less likely given the ascending colon location and lack of appendiceal findings. Typhlitis typically occurs in neutropenic patients, but this patient has leukopenia, yet the procedure context and culture results favor peritonitis.
response.rationale: The clinical scenario of post-endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) with progressive abdominal pain, fever, CT showing bowel wall thickening and ascites, positive E. coli culture, and histology demonstrating acute inflammation and abscesses strongly indicates post-procedure peritonitis. The absence of radiological free air does not rule out microperforation. Perforated appendicitis is unlikely due to the ascending colon location and lack of appendiceal involvement. Typhlitis is associated with neutropenia and typically involves the cecum, but the procedure history and culture results make peritonitis the most probable diagnosis.
